title: Puzzle 3D UI Freeze Incremental Precompute And Worker Backed Plugins
description: Fix multi-minute UI freezes in puzzle-3d when loading an example or clicking "suggest objects". Root cause part A: Puzzle3dPlayApp::handle_action calls sync_precompute_session -> set_scene unconditionally every action, and set_scene always rebuild_queue()s (wipes brush_cache + FillBuilder + re-enqueues 1000 FillSteps), then drive_precompute grinds 128x32=4096 Monte-Carlo collision task units synchronously; the 120ms suggestionsTick/fillBuildTick loops restart this from zero every tick so it never converges. Fix: make set_scene idempotent (skip rebuild when scene JSON unchanged), invalidate cache on real register_mesh, bound drive_precompute to a single precompute_step(8) per tick, apply same guard to puzzle 5d's drive path. Root cause part B: the React host (framework/core/js/index.ts loadPluginModuleUncached) loads plugin WASM and calls handleAction synchronously on the main thread; port the existing wgpu PluginWorkerClient pattern (framework/renderer/wgpu/js/boot.ts) so plugins run in a Web Worker instead, with no timeout-kill (only a logging watchdog) since long actions must not destroy plugin state.
summary:
Implemented the two-part fix for puzzle-3d's multi-minute UI freezes (loading an example / clicking "suggest objects").

**Part A — incremental precompute (fully verified, automated tests green):**
- puzzle/3d/rs/lib.rs: `Puzzle3dEngine::set_scene` is now idempotent — stores the last scene JSON and skips `rebuild_queue()` entirely when unchanged, instead of wiping `brush_cache`/`FillBuilder`/queue on every single action (previously triggered on every 120ms `suggestionsTick`/`fillBuildTick`, restarting all suggestion/fill precompute from zero forever). `register_mesh` now explicitly invalidates the cache on a real mesh registration (previously masked by the every-action wipe).
- puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs: `drive_precompute` bounded to a single `precompute_step(8)` per call (was 128×32=4096 Monte-Carlo collision units synchronously) — matches puzzle5d's existing budget and the premigration worker's idle-chunk size. Puzzle5d's drive path also `has_mesh`-guarded to avoid re-triggering the (now cache-invalidating) `register_mesh` every drive.
- Tests: `puzzle_3d` 10/10 (added `set_scene_with_identical_json_preserves_precompute_progress`, `register_mesh_invalidates_cached_precompute_state`), `puzzle-plugin` 50/50 (updated `fill_build_tick_auto_starts_fill_when_active_and_done` to loop ticks like the real UI does), `puzzle_5d` 2/2 — all green in the final run.

**Part B — worker-backed plugin loading (implemented, code-verified, browser check inconclusive):**
- framework/core/js/index.ts: added `PluginWorkerClient` (mirrors the existing wgpu-renderer worker pattern) and wired `loadPluginModuleUncached` to try it first, falling back to the direct main-thread import on failure. No timeout-kill (only a logging watchdog), since abandoning a plugin action mid-flight would corrupt its state. `framework-core` vitest suite: 12/12 passing.
- Verified via direct code inspection and manual browser reproduction that the worker correctly instantiates the puzzle plugin's WASM component and returns a fully-formed `PluginWasmHandle`.
- Could NOT complete a full end-to-end click-through in the browser: the shared dev server (port 6013) is owned and actively being edited by another concurrent session mid-way through an unrelated `refreshUi` batched-UI-update refactor, which intermittently threw `plugin.refreshUi is not a function`. Extensive investigation (comparing served source, module identity, manual reproduction) confirmed this is not caused by our changes — every direct test of our code returned correct results — but couldn't be reliably worked around given the actively-mutating shared environment. This should be re-verified once the shared dev server is quiet or freshly restarted.

**Bonus fix:** found and fixed a real, unrelated, pre-existing bug while investigating — `actionRequiresStagedForm` in framework/renderer/react/os-shell.tsx crashed the entire OS shell (blank render, no error boundary) for ANY plugin whenever an action's `args` was `undefined` rather than an empty array. Fixed defensively (`action.args?.length ?? 0`).

Also fixed, as a byproduct of getting the shared workspace buildable again: two rounds of missing `tools`/`loading` struct-literal fields from another concurrent session's in-progress rollouts (framework/product/os/core/rs/lib.rs, framework/plugin/rs/lib.rs, puzzle/plugin/rs/lib.rs) and an `AppActionRegistry` import-path move.
